summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, prior CABG, and anxiety presented with recurrent epigastric and substernal pressure that began after she stopped taking Prilosec due to financial constraints. She reported increased anxiety and social stressors, including concerns about financial exploitation by her tenant. Initial evaluation in the ED showed stable vital signs, no ischemic EKG changes, and negative cardiac enzymes across three tests. A chest X-ray revealed no acute findings, and an echocardiogram showed normal ejection fraction with mild mitral regurgitation. A stress test demonstrated normal myocardial perfusion without ischemic changes. Her symptoms were attributed to gastroesophageal reflux, and she was restarted on Prilosec with a prescription covered by insurance. Her Toprol was switched to the extended-release formulation. Social work evaluated her situation and initiated a report for possible elder financial abuse. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider and to return if cardiac symptoms developed.
